more_card_1_text: I’m endlessly curious about the world. New cities, new food, new languages, new tiny details most people overlook. Planning a trip for me is mapping experiences, researching neighborhoods, finding that local spot you won’t see on the first page of Google (or instagram). Traveling feeds my creativity and keeps my brain wide open and my stomach full of delicious food :P
timeline_1_description:
Produced and shaped video content for the institute’s learning platform and digital presence, overseeing the full creative process from filming to post-production. Responsible for shooting, editing, sound design, motion graphics, and delivery.

Led the production and post-production workflow of 12 video podcast episodes, contributing to the core creative and editorial development of the series. Final publication and finishing were completed after my time at the institute.
timeline_2_description:
Managed social media content production, overseeing video creation, motion graphics, and explainer formats across platforms.

Built and executed a niche-focused content strategy, positioning unconventional gaming content effectively on Instagram and TikTok. Created engaging social videos blending motion graphics and explainer storytelling.
timeline_3_description:
During my six-month internship at Hide The Zebra, I edited branded video content for Weber using DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, and After Effects.

I turned recipe videos into engaging stories rather than just step-by-step instructions, and supported motion graphics and color grading across multiple projects.
intro_paragraph_2_html: My style is a chaotic blend of bold pop-culture references, retro nostalgia, and razor-sharp timing. Whether it's a movie documentary or a flash_on social ad, I make sure your audience can't look away.
intro_paragraph_1_html: Hi, I'm Sara. I'm a video editor who believes in the rhythm of the cut. I don't just assemble clips; I orchestrate emotions.
more_card_3_text: I’m a nerd, unapologetically. I love tech, new tools, new platforms, and especially the challenges that come with them. I get genuinely excited when something breaks and I get to figure it out. I started planning a Southeast Asia trip with an over-the-top Google Sheet… and somehow ended up designing and deploying my own travel-planning app.
more_card_2_text: I’ve been doing pole for over four years and I teach it with the same intensity I train. Even when my muscles are begging for mercy, I still want one more climb, one more spin, one more attempt at the trick that scared me yesterday. Pole is strength, discipline, bruises, music, and pure adrenaline. It’s the place where I test my limits and then move them
